summary_of_core_decisions: Knauff argues that van Inwagen's reductio against DAUP fails because it equivocates on 'Descartes' between an abstract sense (the man as a persisting entity) and a material sense (the body or its parts). When the four identities are disambiguated, the apparent violation of transitivity of identity disappears. Thus, DAUP is not refuted by van Inwagen's argument.
